articles.title: Former skipper Suryakumar admits India snub after winning T20 World Cup 2026 was 'very difficult' - WION
articles.summary: Former skipper Suryakumar admits India snub after winning T20 World Cup 2026 was 'very difficult' WION
articles.content: Former India T20I skipper Suryakumar Yadav, who has lost his captaincy and place in the side, admitted that the period after the T20 World Cup 2026 has been difficult. SKY, as he is fondly called, lost his place and captaincy despite taking India to T20 World Cup glory at home in March earlier this year. He has since played only in the IPL and was not even selected for Mumbai's Ranji Trophy squad because of a lack of preparation for red-ball games. He has been, however, named Mumbai captain for the domestic T20 tournament, the Syed Mushtaq Ali Trophy, which starts on November 14. SKY ready to bounce back from India snub "Post the T20 World Cup, it has been a little difficult," SKY acknowledged at an MCA event in Mumbai on Tuesday (Nov 10). "I don't want to run away from the fact: if you're not honest with yourself, it's very difficult to lead a happy life. To be very honest, it has been very difficult. The first two months after the IPL were difficult, but then I thought, why not think about how I was before - how I started my cricket, when I used to think I wanted to play age-group cricket for Mumbai, I wanted to play first-class cricket for Mumbai." he said. Also Read - Rishabh Pant set for final fitness clearance ahead of New Zealand departure What next for SKY? With the Mumbai Indians reportedly trading Hardik Pandya, SKY is definitely one of the contenders to lead the side in IPL 2027. The batter, however, isn't thinking too far ahead and is focused on what he "did 10-15 years ago - training again, following the same passion, same love for this game and everything is back to normal. When you start thinking about it, and you're focused on playing the sport, you want to do well for your team and your family; things change completely. And that's what I'm doing right now. The main goal is what I used to think before - to win the championship for Mumbai." Mumbai play all their SMAT matches in Kolkata and are strong favorites to win the tournament.

articles.title: Usman Khawaja cancels book interviews after TV appearance goes horribly wrong - India Today
articles.summary: Usman Khawaja cancels book interviews after TV appearance goes horribly wrong India Today
articles.content: Under-fire Usman Khawaja has pulled out of TV and book interviews after his chat with broadcaster Sarah Ferguson went horribly wrong on Tuesday, November 10.Khawaja, who was on the show to promote his new book, Sabr, was grilled by the ABC broadcaster on the 7.30 programme about his claims surrounding the Sandpapergate controversy. Khawaja ducked the majority of the questions, which were related to his now-viral revelations about Australia's tour of South Africa in 2018.Khawaja's meek interview copped widespread criticism online, with many hitting out at the former Australian batter for failing to speak up during the television appearance.After the interview, Australian media reports suggest that Khawaja has not only declined to do further TV interviews but has also cancelled several book-related interviews.ABC Sport reported that Penguin, Khawaja's publisher, confirmed there would be adjustments to his book tour and interview commitments, although it did not clarify exactly which appearances had been affected."The book tour is 100 (per cent) still going ahead, we've just had to make some adjustments this week but no major cancellation of the tour at all," the publisher said in a statement.KHAWAJA DUCKS THE WARNER QUESTIONKhawaja's appearance on the ABC's 7.30 programme was supposed to be an opportunity to promote his book and explain his account of the infamous 2018 South Africa tour. Instead, it turned into an uncomfortable exchange as Ferguson repeatedly pressed him on some of the most controversial claims in Sabr.At the centre of the controversy is Khawaja's suggestion that the ball-tampering scandal in Cape Town was not limited to the three players who were eventually punished. He has argued that more members of the Australian team knew about the use of sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball, including during the preceding Test in Port Elizabeth.Khawaja has stopped short of naming individuals, insisting that he is simply sharing what he witnessed and experienced. However, his account has raised questions about the involvement and knowledge of several former teammates.Ferguson began by bringing up David Warner's public support for Khawaja's version of events. The former Australia opener had also suggested that lies would eventually come out, prompting the broadcaster to ask Khawaja what lies he was referring to."I'm not going to speak on behalf of Davey. I've tried my best to tell my story in an open and safe environment. There's no easy way to do it, but I mean, I'm not here to inflame the situation any more," Khawaja responded.He maintained that he was only trying to share his version of events and stand by Warner, Steve Smith and Cameron Bancroft, the three players who were punished following the scandal.KHAWAJA ON THE BACKFOOTFerguson then turned to a joint statement issued by Australia's four frontline bowlers, Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon, in 2021. The quartet had denied knowing that sandpaper was being taken onto the field during the Cape Town Test.Khawaja, who has written in his book that he was unhappy with the bowlers' statement, was asked whether their account was incorrect.He refused to give a direct answer, instead reiterating that he had already shared what he knew about the preceding Test in Port Elizabeth."I'll say again, I've given my statement about what happened the game before. I was very open and honest to what I saw and what conversations I had," he said.Khawaja also admitted that he had deliberately been vague about certain aspects of his account."Sometimes I'm very specific on things and sometimes I'm a bit vague on things and I do it on purpose because I'm trying to tell a story," he said.Ferguson pressed further, asking whether the four bowlers had been involved in conversations about ball tampering."I'm just not going I'm not going to entertain that," Khawaja replied.KHAWAJA DODGES DIRECT QUESTION ON CUMMINSThe most uncomfortable exchange came when Ferguson directly asked whether Cummins, Australia's current Test captain, had prior knowledge of sandpaper being used to alter the ball."I'm not going to answer that," Khawaja said.He added that he had written what he wanted to in his book and had already shared his account of the events. Khawaja also referred to former teammate Chadd Sayers, who had recently backed some of his claims.However, Ferguson pointed out the contradiction in Khawaja's position. While he insisted he was not pointing fingers, his account suggested that responsibility for the scandal extended beyond the three players who were punished.She also asked whether the wider Australian playing group and coaching staff had prior knowledge of the use of sandpaper.Khawaja again avoided a direct answer, saying he had told his story and hoped others would come forward and speak honestly."I mean, I've written in my account from what I've seen. People want to know the answers and lots of different answers. And I've left it open-ended to some respects because I've told my story and I've told my truth and I'll speak for myself," he said."I'm hoping other people will come up and talk about it honestly. That's what I'm hoping. But I'm not forcing anyone to do anything."NOT CONDUCTING A WITCH-HUNT: KHAWAJAThroughout the interview, Khawaja maintained that he was not conducting a witch-hunt against his former teammates and was not calling for Cricket Australia to reopen its investigation into the scandal.He also stood by his view that the bans handed to Smith, Warner and Bancroft were excessive. Smith and Warner received 12-month suspensions, while Bancroft was banned for nine months."I'm not calling for anything. I'm literally sharing my version of the truth," Khawaja said.Cricket Australia, meanwhile, maintained that it remained comfortable with the findings of its original investigation, while acknowledging that there were differing recollections of some events."The three players who received bans after the Cape Town Test acknowledged their breaches and accepted the penalties imposed," a CA spokesperson said."We have acknowledged that the investigation was conducted in a short timeframe given the impending Test match and that there are varying opinions about some matters including the length of the sanctions imposed. We respect that players have different recollections of events from this time."But we remain comfortable the investigation's findings accurately reflect the statements and evidence provided at the time."Ferguson also questioned Khawaja about his suggestion that racial prejudice may have played a role in him not being considered for Australia's interim captaincy in Smith's absence in 2018.Khawaja admitted that he had no concrete evidence to support the claim, explaining that it was based on how he felt at the time.The broadcaster also asked about his relationship with Cummins, given the Australian captain's reputation has been caught up in the controversy."I'm not sure," Khawaja replied. "But I've been friends with Pat a long time. I've told my truth and I've given my reasons at the end of the day. I think some things I've always stood for - my values and what I think is right. Yeah, there's no ideal way of doing this, but I can't speak for Pat."- Ends

articles.title: India snub hit hard, but Suryakumar Yadav is rediscovering love, passion for cricket - India Today
articles.summary: India snub hit hard, but Suryakumar Yadav is rediscovering love, passion for cricket India Today
articles.content: Being dropped from the team you once led is never easy. Finding the motivation to pick yourself up and fight your way back can be even harder. For Suryakumar Yadav, the blow was particularly painful. articles.title: Chennai set to bring Asian Athletics Championships back to India in 2029 - India Today
articles.summary: Chennai set to bring Asian Athletics Championships back to India in 2029 India Today
articles.content: Chennai is on the verge of securing the rights to host the 2029 Asian Athletics Championships, with the Asian Athletics Association (AAA) awaiting formal assurances from the Tamil Nadu government before making the award official.The continental body's council discussed the proposal at its 107th meeting in Tokyo on Tuesday. The final confirmation is expected once the state government submits the required financial and administrative guarantees.“Subject to presentation of letters of guarantee from the Govt, Asian Athletics Association is pleased to award the 2029 Asian Athletics Championships to Chennai, Tamil Nadu,” the statement read.C Latha, a senior official of the Tamil Nadu Athletics Association who is in Tokyo as part of the Indian contingent, said the documents were expected to be handed over on Wednesday."We have made the presentation and the Asian Athletics Association (AAA) asked us to submit the financial and other guarantees from the state government. The AAA said they will award the 2029 Asian Championships to Chennai once they get the guarantees," Latha told PTI from Tokyo."We are hoping to get the guarantees tomorrow from our state government. So, the final decision is expected to come tomorrow," she added.World Athletics Vice President and Athletics Federation of India (AFI) spokesperson Adille Sumariwalla was also present at the meeting. He confirmed that Chennai would be awarded the hosting rights once the necessary guarantees were received from the state government.If finalised, the event will mark the third occasion that India has staged the Asian Athletics Championships. Pune hosted the competition in 2013, followed by Bhubaneswar in 2017. Chennai is set to welcome the 28th edition of the biennial event in 2029.The next edition, the 27th in the series, is scheduled to take place in Xiamen, China, between May 28 and June 2, 2027.India is also preparing to stage several major athletics competitions over the coming years. Chandigarh is scheduled to host the Asian Relays Championships in August 2027, while Bhubaneswar will stage both the Asian Indoor Athletics Championships and the World Indoor Athletics Championships in 2028.The country is also in the race to bring the World U20 Athletics Championships to Ahmedabad in 2028.- Ends

articles.title: Owaisi Questions Maharashtra Govt’s UCC Questionnaire - Deccan Chronicle
articles.summary: Owaisi Questions Maharashtra Govt’s UCC Questionnaire Deccan Chronicle
articles.content: Hyderabad: AIMIM President Asaduddin Owaisi has said the Maharashtra government has invited opinions from the public to implement UCC and it has also prepared a questionnaire for it. The questionnaire, prepared by the Maharashtra government, makes it clear that the Devendra Fadnavis government will implement the UCC. The questionnaire consists of leading questions on polygamy and extra-judicial divorce. But there is not one question on Hindu Undivided Family. This makes it evident that, much like the initiatives introduced by BJP governments in Gujarat, Uttarakhand, Assam, and Madhya Pradesh under the guise of a 'Uniform Civil Code,' this is not a true UCC, but rather a 'Hindu Civil Code' that is being imposed upon non-Hindu communities. “Additionally, if you examine the questionnaire, you will find that the majority of the questions are framed in a 'yes or no' format. I believe this is precisely why R.C. Chavan, a retired judge of the Bombay High Court, chose to resign,” he explained. He had stated that there is no one from the minority community. They are talking about implementation in Maharashtra at this juncture, but they are not defining what this 'uniform' actually is."

articles.summary: India's Pollution Crisis Hits Sports: Chennai Open Tennis Final Postponed Amid Heavy Smog Business Today
articles.content: India's post-Diwali pollution surge has disrupted more than just daily life. The Chennai Open women's singles final between defending champion Janice Tien and Magda Linette was postponed after rain delays were followed by heavy smoke from Diwali fireworks engulfing the stadium. Tien shared an Instagram story showing the smog and an AQI reading of 1,556, raising fresh concerns over the conditions at the venue. The incident adds to a growing list of sporting events affected by India's pollution crisis, including cricket fixtures that have faced postponements or venue changes amid poor air quality. As the Chennai Open approaches its final edition, the disruption has cast a shadow over the tournament's farewell.

articles.title: What is the Gokul Cooperative Milk Federation election issue in Maharashtra? | Explained - The Hindu
articles.summary: What is the Gokul Cooperative Milk Federation election issue in Maharashtra? | Explained The Hindu
articles.content: Election to one of Maharashtra’s largest milk federations has turned into a political slugfest. Kolhapur Zilla Sahakari Dudh Utpadak Sangh Ltd, known as Gokul, is one of Maharashtra’s largest and most influential dairy co-operatives. After the election to the directors’ positions was held recently, the Congress-led panel won by a wafer-thin majority of 13-12 in a body of 25 directors. Soon thereafter, the BJP-led State government passed an order to appoint five nominated directors. Four of them will have voting rights. This caused a massive backlash, as it will tilt the majority in favour of the ruling alliance via nominated directors, though the alliance could not garner a majority through a democratically held election. Kolhapur Zilla Sahakari Dudh Utpadak Sangh Ltd., well known for its popular brand ‘Gokul ’, is an Operation Flood cooperative dairy project established on March 16, 1963. It is one of the most significant political and economic forces in western Maharashtra and has established itself as a prime dairy co-operative in the State. Maharashtra’s politics is shaped by the significant co-operatives’ sector.

articles.title: Farmers protest in Kolhapur against Maharashtra government's Gokul board move - The New Indian Express
articles.summary: Farmers protest in Kolhapur against Maharashtra government's Gokul board move The New Indian Express
articles.content: MUMBAI: Thousands of milk-producing farmers took to the streets against the BJP-led Maharashtra government in Kolhapur, protesting and demanding the rescinding of the state government's decision to give voting rights to four directors appointed to the Gokul Milk Federation.Congress leader Satej Patil and farmer leader Raju Shetty organised the massive protest under the banner of the Sangharsh Morcha, where dairy farmers from across Kolhapur district, along with supporters from neighbouring Sangli and Satara, participated in the march at Dasara Chowk in Kolhapur.During the protest, several farmers brought their cattle, underlining their opposition to what they described as government interference in a cooperative institution built around milk producers. Local lawyers also participated, carrying black flags and banners opposing the government's decision.The protest came against the backdrop of the Maharashtra Cabinet's November 4 decision to amend the Maharashtra Cooperative Societies Act, 1960, allowing the government to nominate five members to the managing committees of cooperative institutions with an annual turnover exceeding Rs 500 crore.Of the five nominees, four will have voting rights, while the fifth will be a government officer not below the rank of assistant registrar without voting rights. The nominated members, however, will not be eligible to contest elections for office-bearer posts..Bombay HC refuses to stay Gokul Chairman polls; four govt-nominated directors allowed to cast votes.The government's decision has triggered a major controversy because of the recent Gokul board elections held on October 19. The Congress-led Samvichari Aghadi won 13 of the 25 seats, while the BJP-led Mahayuti panel secured 12. The outcome gave the opposition-backed panel a narrow majority in the influential dairy cooperative, which has an annual turnover of more than Rs 4,000 crore.Opposition leaders allege that the government has introduced the amendment to alter the electoral arithmetic after the Mahayuti failed to secure a majority. With four government-nominated members enjoying voting rights, the ruling alliance could potentially increase its strength from 12 to 16, against the 13 elected Congress-led panel directors.The Opposition alleged that the state government's decision was an attempt to overturn the mandate of nearly 5.5 lakh milk producers represented through the cooperative's electoral process.The controversy intensified after the election of Gokul's chairman was stalled because of a lack of quorum. Under the cooperative's bylaws, at least 14 directors are required to be present for the chairman's election. The 12 Mahayuti-backed directors remained absent from the earlier meeting, preventing the 13-member opposition-backed group from completing the process.Meanwhile, the Bombay High Court refused to stay the state government's decision and allowed the election of Gokul chairman on November 10, 2026. The court asked that the votes of state government-appointed directors be kept in a sealed cover. The entire election process must also be video-recorded. The election result will be declared, but its validity will remain subject to the final outcome of the court proceedings scheduled for November 25..Gokul takeover row: Maharashtra move to appoint five directors sparks political clash.Follow The New Indian Express channel on WhatsApp Download the TNIE app to stay with us and follow the latest
